source.title: Resurrecting the Salmon: Rethinking Mechanistic Interpretability with Domain-Specific Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Charles O'Neill; M. Jayasekara; Max Kirkby

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses feature splitting and absorption, but its own experiments do not test whether larger dictionaries split coarse features or whether split features partition the same inputs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own feature-matching analysis between GemmaScope and domain-specific SAE features, recorded below as an adjacent finding. Its reconstruction, interpretability, and residual-error results do not measure feature splitting, nested feature families, or absorption. Statements about splitting in wider SAEs cite prior work rather than report this study's own test.
record.test_reason: The paper's own experiments compare domain-specific JumpReLU SAEs with GemmaScope SAEs on reconstruction, loss recovered, autointerp F1 and dark-matter metrics. It trains Gemma-2-9b SAEs at widths 2^14 to 2^20 but reports no analysis of coarse features splitting across widths, feature families, parent/child absorption, or objective comparisons. Statements that splitting and absorption worsen in wider SAEs, and that domain confinement mitigates fragmentation, cite prior work or are asserted without a measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that domain-confined (medical) SAEs on Gemma-2 layer 20 explain 15–20% more variance, recover more loss, leave less linearly predictable dark matter, and give more interpretable features than GemmaScope. They assert, without measuring it, that this mitigates feature fragmentation. The Discussion also claims steering results that the text does not report.
record.recipe_differences: Trains JumpReLU SAEs on medical-domain activations and compares them with GemmaScope; it does not apply a feature-splitting measurement across increasing dictionary sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper varies SAE width and target sparsity for its reconstruction and residual-error evaluations, but does not report how these settings affect feature splitting.

fits_no_version.finding: Many GemmaScope features have matched counterparts in the domain-specific SAE that are similar in both decoder and encoder space. A smaller group of matches maps to different indices in the two spaces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features partly correspond across training-data domains at equal width; some correspondences are inconsistent between encoder and decoder.

record.problems: The feature-matching result is qualitative, and the paper does not report numerical values or uncertainty for it. Its own experiments do not test the claim versions about splitting, absorption, or objective artifacts.
record.rows_left_out: Reconstruction fidelity, loss recovery, interpretability scores, and dark-matter analyses are not rows because they do not measure feature splitting or the other behaviors specified by the claim. Prior-work results discussed in the paper are not this study's results.

untested.parts: All: no coarse-to-fine comparison across widths, no input-coverage or directional-proximity measure, although multiple widths were trained.
All: no splitting measurement on Gemma-2 or GemmaScope.
All: no nested-family or hierarchy analysis.
All: absorption is only cited (Chanin et al.); no parent/child firing measurement and no size or sparsity sweep for absorption.
All: no decomposition of larger-SAE latents into smaller-SAE latents and no count of novel latents.
All: the sparsity-penalty explanation is cited (Anders et al., Till); no objective comparison. The training-domain manipulation is not measured for splitting.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T6/discusses classification is right. The paper's mentions of splitting and absorption (Introduction, Related Work, Discussion) all cite Chanin et al. 2024, Till 2024 and Anders et al. 2024. The steering evaluations claimed in the Discussion do not appear in the results. Appendix E is empty.

versions.untested_parts: No same-activation dictionary-size comparison measuring coarse-to-fine splitting, input coverage, or directional proximity.
No test of splitting across large models or open SAE releases.
No test of nested split-feature families or whether they mirror a conceptual hierarchy.
No measurement of parent-child coactivation, missed parent activations, or whether size or sparsity changes absorption.
No size-controlled test of larger SAE latents decomposing into smaller SAE latents or adding novel latents.
No test attributing splitting to the SAE objective or comparing objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: GemmaScope SAE vs. our domain-specific SAE
rows.operation_detail: Hungarian matching of SAE encoder and decoder feature vectors by cosine similarity

conditions.value: GemmaScope features matched to features in the domain-specific SAE

rows.measure: Matched encoder- and decoder-space cosine similarity and whether the matches point to the same feature index
rows.value: Most points with high decoder similarity also have high encoder similarity; a smaller group of matches is inconsistent across the two spaces.
rows.note: This compares features across SAE datasets, not features across increasing dictionary sizes; it does not identify split families or test input partitioning.
rows.check: Cross-SAE feature matching (GemmaScope vs domain SAE) via Hungarian cosine similarity. It is not a dictionary-size comparison and identifies no split families. The text describes it only qualitatively, so the value is correct as text and no number can be read.

rows.subject: Our domain-specific SAE and GemmaScope SAE
rows.operation_detail: Distribution of maximum cosine similarities for learned SAE features
rows.note: The figure gives distributions but the paper does not describe their values in text; it is not a dictionary-size splitting test.
rows.check: Figure 9 gives max-cosine distributions for the two SAEs with no text values, so nothing can be read. It does not bear on splitting.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
